# R749SOZ — A full exact 1/25-area zero-gap Walsh triangle

Date: 2026-11-14. Classification: AUTHOR_EXACT_NOT_REVIEWED. Science frozen at awdawmip/enterprise-math@a72226e2430ffa4786321ac86e7f0c599d5f0389. This is an auxiliary Walsh observer calculation, not an assertion about native X6 cells, directions, time, or an X6/V29/V39 correspondence.

## Question and theorem

Following R749SOX–SOY (Draft PR #2409, immutable scientific commit 1499ed88bcc5f23c2b1fcd77ed9d5c00e8779807), determine a larger exact two-parameter zero-calibration-gap region around the previously proved 1/200-area rectangle.

Let K=F_2^4 with chi_m(k)=(-1)^popcount(k&m). Put A=chi_3, B=chi_12, C=chi_15=AB and define the complete compatible source fiber

\[
F_{t,s}=\left\{p_{t,s,h,u,v,w,z}(k)=
\frac{1+tA(k)+sB(k)+hC(k)+u\chi_1(k)+v\chi_2(k)+w\chi_4(k)+z\chi_8(k)}{16}\ge0\ (\forall k)\right\}.
\]

Normalization follows from character orthogonality. Define the free radius rho(t,s)=inf over all probability centers q of sup over p in F(t,s) TV(p,q), the calibrated radius rho_cal(t,s)=inf over q in F(t,s) of the same worst-case risk, and gap g=rho_cal-rho. The total-variation convention is TV(p,q)=sum_k |p(k)-q(k)|/2.

**Theorem R749SOZ (all real parameters).** Let

\[
T=\operatorname{conv}\{(3/10,1/2),(2/5,3/5),(0,1)\}
=\{(t,s):5t+3s\ge3,\ 5(s-t)\ge1,\ t+s\le1\}.
\]

For every real (t,s) in the complete closed triangle T,

\[
\boxed{\rho(t,s)=\rho_{\rm cal}(t,s)=(3-t+s)/8,\qquad g(t,s)=0.}
\]

An explicitly optimal **calibrated** center is q(t,s)=p(t,s,0,0,0,0,0). This triangle has area exactly 1/25, eight times the area of the R749SOY zero-gap rectangle (1/200). That rectangle is contained in T: its four corners satisfy the three inequalities.

## Lower certificate: two source laws and an exact TV diameter

For every (t,s) in T take

\[
P_+=p(t,s,0,t,t,1-t,s),\qquad
P_-=p(t,s,0,-t,-t,t-1,-s).
\]

All sixteen atom probabilities of each law are affine in (t,s). At the three parameter vertices the accompanying Fraction checker verifies their nonnegativity and sums of one. The entire triangle is their convex hull, hence both laws belong to F(t,s) throughout T.

For each k, the difference P_+(k)-P_-(k) is affine in (t,s). Its signs at the three corners are pairwise consistent (nonnegative products, with zeros permitted), which fixes the sign over T. Consequently TV(P_+,P_-) is affine in (t,s) throughout T. The three exact corner evaluations are: TV=4/5 at (3/10,1/2), TV=4/5 at (2/5,3/5), and TV=1 at (0,1). Therefore

\[
\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)=\frac{3-t+s}{4}\quad \text{on }T.
\]

For any center q, the TV triangle inequality gives max(TV(P_+,q),TV(P_-,q)) >= TV(P_+,P_-)/2. Thus rho(t,s) >= (3-t+s)/8.

## Upper certificate: complete exact seven-dimensional joint-polytope enumeration

The center q(t,s) is nonnegative because T has t>=0, s>=0, t+s<=1. It lies in F(t,s). Consider the compact joint source polytope J in variables x=(t,s,h,u,v,w,z), cut out by 16 normalized source inequalities

\[
1+tA(k)+sB(k)+hC(k)+u\chi_1(k)+v\chi_2(k)+w\chi_4(k)+z\chi_8(k)\ge0,\quad k=0,\ldots,15,
\]

and by the three triangle inequalities

\[
5t+3s\ge3,\quad -5t+5s\ge1,\quad -t-s\ge-1.
\]

It is bounded because every Walsh coefficient is the expectation of a sign character of a nonnegative normalized law, and full-dimensional because the triangle and source fiber have simultaneous strict interior points.

Every vertex is the unique intersection of seven linearly independent active constraints. The attached pure-standard-library program enumerates *all* C(19,7)=50,388 seven-constraint combinations, solves them by integer Bareiss elimination with exact Fraction back substitution, filters every one of the 19 inequalities, and de-duplicates exact vertices. Observed machine-checkable counts:

- Nonsingular active bases: 28,288.
- Feasible bases (with multiplicity): 4,944.
- Distinct rational vertices: 70.
- Exact tight risk vertices: 26.
- Maximal TV(p_x,q_{t,s})-(3-t+s)/8 among all distinct vertices: **0**.

All 70 exact vertices passed source/center normalization and nonnegativity. The unique parameter values of those vertices were (0,1), (1/3,2/3), (2/5,3/5), (3/10,1/2), (3/13,8/13), with the complete counts in the JSON result.

The function x -> TV(p_x,q_{t,s})-(3-t+s)/8 is convex: every atomwise difference is affine in x, absolute value is convex, and subtraction of an affine term preserves convexity. Any point of compact J is a convex combination of its vertices. The verified vertex inequalities therefore prove the **universal real-parameter upper bound** TV(p,q(t,s)) <= (3-t+s)/8 for every (t,s) in T and every p in F(t,s). Combined with the lower certificate and q in F(t,s), this establishes both exact minimax identities.

The finite enumeration proves a precisely identified finite vertex claim; the continuum statement follows from the separate compact-polytope/convexity proof. This is an author-side exact proof and has not received independent mathematical review.

## Strict nearby obstruction for this particular center

At (t,s)=(1/5,3/5), outside T across the facet 5t+3s=3, choose the feasible law

\[
p_*=p(1/5,3/5,-1/5,0,0,4/5,4/5).
\]

Its 16 atom masses are nonnegative and sum to one. Direct Fraction computation gives

\[
\operatorname{TV}(p_*,q(1/5,3/5))=9/20>17/40=(3-1/5+3/5)/8.
\]

Thus the same zero-additional-coefficient center does not satisfy this *specific triangular radius formula* at that point. This observation leaves the globally optimal free/calibrated radii there to be determined by other centers. No zero/positive gap assertion is inferred from this one-center obstruction.

## Reproduction and continuation

Files saved together at this immutable scientific commit:
(1) this full manuscript; (2) R749SOZ_WALSH_ZERO_TRIANGLE_CERT.py; (3) R749SOZ_WALSH_ZERO_TRIANGLE_RESULTS.json.

Reproduction: Python 3 standard library only; run the program and compare the complete JSON output with the saved result. The 7D exact joint polytope handles every compatible 16-atom source: no sampling, floating-point acceptance, or undocumented source reduction. R749SOX–SOY's exact four-branch BRC observer reduction may be reused, but is not needed for the exhaustive proof here. The proof is internal to the frozen auxiliary observer. Native X6/V29/V39 observer-preserving transfer remains a separate open research objective.

**Next scientific question:** find piecewise optimal center coefficients near the triangular facet 5t+3s=3, and distinguish (i) failure of the explicit q_0 center, (ii) failure of the proposed radius formula, and (iii) a genuinely positive calibration gap. Then seek independent review of the exact 7D certificate and any native correspondence separately.
